currentDelivery.attachment:
# Sharing course materials on Zedu: permission and attribution guide

*Capture date: 23 Oct 2026. Public-page facts carry URL and date; app-only steps are marked [CONFIRM].*

## 1. File upload permissions

- Upload files into a channel so they stay with the conversation and class where they belong. (Source: https://zedu.chat/products/file-management, "Share files directly in channels to keep context and discussions connected", captured 23 Oct 2026.)
- Store lectures, assignments and resources in one central workspace, organised by course, department or cohort for easy access. (Source: https://zedu.chat/products/file-management, "Store Course Materials in Organized Spaces", captured 23 Oct 2026.)
- File sharing is available on every plan, including Starter. "Shared Resources" is only listed on the paid plans, so check /pricing before promising shared resource folders to a Starter cohort. (Source: https://zedu.chat/pricing, "Plan Features" table, captured 23 Oct 2026.)
- Permissions are controlled through "Workspace Permissions" and "Admin Controls" (Basic on Starter, Advanced on Pro). (Source: https://zedu.chat/pricing, captured 23 Oct 2026.)
- Role names used on the public pages are teachers/admins and students, not "organiser, instructor, learner". (Source: https://zedu.chat/pricing, captured 23 Oct 2026.)

## 2. Channel-level access

- Create a channel per cohort or subject so materials are scoped to the right audience. (Source: task brief; channel scoping [CONFIRM in live app].)
- Share files directly inside class discussions so context and chat stay connected. (Source: https://zedu.chat/products/file-management, captured 23 Oct 2026.)
- Pin the key document in the channel so everyone finds the current version. [CONFIRM: pinning in live app.]
- Keep drafts or answer keys in a restricted channel until release. [CONFIRM: restricted channels exist as described.]

## 3. Attribution best practices

- Name the author and source of every shared file in the message or pin.
- Include a short credit line: "Source: [name], [title], [link], used with permission."
- Keep a "Resources" or "Credits" note in the channel listing all shared materials and their sources.
- Ask before resharing third-party content; store the permission note with the file.

## 4. Template for crediting sources

```
Title: [Material name]
Author / source: [Name or organisation]
Original link: [URL]
Permission: [Granted by / date / conditions]
Shared by: [Your name], [date]
Use: [Which cohort / lesson]
```

## Screenshots

The live app screens for upload, permission toggles and pinning need app access I do not have. Public product images for reference: https://zedu.chat/images/homepage/products/files/image-1.png and https://zedu.chat/images/homepage/products/files/image-2.png (captured 23 Oct 2026). I am escalating for a test workspace so the app screenshots can be captured and swapped in.

## Notes for the team

- Replace [CONFIRM] items with live-app paths and role names once app access is available.
- Do not promise export or download features unless the live app shows them.

changesToCheck.body:
I read the attachment in full and checked the public pages before writing this.

What meets the brief: section 3 on attribution and section 4's crediting template are solid, usable work that needs no app access, and marking unconfirmed items rather than inventing them is the right instinct.

What does not meet it:

1. Screenshots. The task says "Include screenshots from the live app". There are none, and the delivery hands that work back to the team ("Screenshot each permission and sharing step in the live app and replace [CONFIRM] items before publishing"). That is the deliverable, not a note for someone else.

2. Sections 1 and 2 have no verified content. Every line about upload permissions and channel access is sourced to "task brief" with [CONFIRM] attached, so the two sections the task names first tell an educator nothing they can act on. The role names "organiser, instructor, learner" are invented shapes - the public pages say teachers/admins and students, and /pricing lists "Workspace Permissions" and "Admin Controls" (Basic on Starter, Advanced on the paid plan) as the permission surfaces that actually exist.

3. Public evidence that was available was not used. /products/file-management states "Organize files by courses, departments, or cohorts for easy access", "Store lectures, assignments, and resources in one central workspace" and "Share files directly in channels to keep context and discussions connected" - checked live today. Those lines support most of section 1 and 2's structure without any [CONFIRM] at all. Note also that /pricing marks "Shared Resources" as not included on Starter while "File Sharing" is on every plan, which a guide about sharing materials should tell the reader.

To fix: add the screenshots the task asks for, or say plainly in the delivery that you have no app access and ask for one via an escalation; replace the [CONFIRM] lines in sections 1 and 2 with what the public pages do state, each with its URL and capture date; correct the role names to the ones the pages use; and add the Starter limit on shared resources.

I read the whole attachment against the four things the task asks for.

What meets the brief: sections 3 and 4. The attribution advice is concrete and usable (name the author and source in the message or pin, keep a Credits note in the channel, ask before resharing third-party content and store the permission note with the file), and the crediting template has every field an educator needs — title, author or source, original link, permission with date and conditions, who shared it, and which cohort. Those two sections I would publish close to as-is.

What does not meet the brief, and how to fix each:

1. Screenshots from the live app. The task says to include them; there are none. The delivery instead hands the job back to the team: "Screenshot each permission and sharing step in the live app and replace [CONFIRM] items before publishing." That is the requirement, not a note for someone else. Fix: add the screenshots as image links in the attachment, one per step (upload into a channel, setting who can upload, setting who can view, pinning). If the attachment cannot carry images, say so in the thread and post the image URLs — and if you have no access to the app, escalate for the test workspace rather than deliver without them.

2. Sections 1 and 2 contain no confirmed information. Every substantive line is marked [CONFIRM] and the stated source is the task brief itself ("Source: task brief; live app paths [CONFIRM]"), so the guide does not yet tell an educator what Zedu actually does. Fix: for each of the four items, give the real path and the exact on-screen names — where files are uploaded, which setting controls who can upload, which controls who can view, and the actual role names. The guide names "organiser, instructor, learner" but marks them unconfirmed; one of those either matches the product or it does not, and the delivery needs to say which.

3. Scope check on one line. "Keep drafts or answer keys in a restricted channel until you are ready to release them" is good advice but depends on restricted channels existing as described. Confirm it or drop it.

Marking what you could not verify is the right instinct and I would rather see [CONFIRM] than invented menu names. The problem is that it covers the half of the guide the task is mainly about. With the screenshots added and sections 1 and 2 carrying real app detail, this becomes a strong approve from me.
